newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian Socialists win 2/3 of vote in elections.
newsitem.headline: Albanian Socialists win 2/3 of vote in elections.

text.p: Albania's ex-communist Socialists and their allies have won a two thirds majority in elections called to end months of anarchy, elections officials said on Wednesday.
The central elections commission said that following two rounds of voting on June 29 and July 6, the Socialist group had won at least 107 of the 155 parliamentary seats.
The sweeping majority will enable a Socialist-led coalition containing five other small parties of the centre and left to push through far-reaching legislation -- and elect a new head of state.
With only a handful of seats still to be decided, the figures show the right-wing Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha trailing badly with under 40 seats.
The Democrats, in power since 1992, won a landslide in elections last May which were boycotted by the opposition and branded as seriously flawed by international monitors.
But the collapse of shady pyramid schemes earlier this year, bankrupting thousands of families, sparked a violent uprising against the government for allowing the schemes to flourish.
